::: {.lead}
*Pocket Quest 1.3* is in the stores, and the reviews arrive: "Smooth on my
new phone!", "It jerks every few seconds", "It closes at once on my old
phone", "The Start button is cut off on my tablet". Some players use phones
that Byte Bay never tested, and a new OS update is coming. In lecture 13
you set up a test environment. In this lesson you study **real cases** of
performance and compatibility: how to measure smoothness, why a build fails
on some devices, and how to follow new platform versions with **reliable
sources**. Every section ends with a short task.
:::

## Key terms

{{< glossary frame-rate frame-time stutter one-percent-low thermal-throttling frame-rate-cap compatibility api-level graphics-api compatibility-matrix release-notes reliable-source >}}

## 14.1 Measuring performance

The average frame rate is not the whole story (@fig-frames).

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 14.1 — Measures of performance"}
- **Frame time:** the time of one frame in milliseconds; 60 fps ≈ 16.7 ms,
  30 fps ≈ 33.3 ms.
- **Average fps:** frames per second over a whole race.
- **1 % low:** the frame rate of the slowest 1 % of frames. A low 1 % low
  means **stutters**: single long frames that the player feels as jerks.
- **Load time, battery use and temperature** complete the picture.

Measure on real devices, with the same test each time, as long as players
play: after some minutes a hot chip slows down (**thermal throttling**,
lecture 3). A **frame-rate cap** (for example 30 fps) or lower settings keep
the game steady.
:::

![Frame times of one race (example values).](images/frame-times.png){#fig-frames width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 14.1 — The jerk of Star Garden"}
1. The counter shows 59 fps on average while a player waters the garden.
2. The frame-time graph shows one frame of 70 ms every 10 seconds: a
   stutter.
3. The developers find that the game saves to the cloud in that frame.
   They save in the background, and the stutter is gone.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Reporting only the average fps. A game with a high average and many
stutters feels worse than a steady 30 fps.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Frame times"}
Compute the frame time of 30, 60 and 120 fps (1000 ms ÷ fps). A frame takes
50 ms: what frame rate would that be if all frames took that long?

*Your result:* four numbers.

::: {.check}
30 fps: 1000 ÷ 30 ≈ 33.3 ms. 60 fps: ≈ 16.7 ms. 120 fps: ≈ 8.3 ms. A
50 ms frame: 1000 ÷ 50 = 20 fps. One such frame in a 60 fps race is a
stutter that the player feels.
:::
:::

## 14.2 Compatibility

A build can fail on some devices even when it runs well on others
(@fig-compat).

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 14.2 — Three causes of incompatibility"}
- **Minimum OS version:** a build made for Android 11 (API 30) cannot start
  on Android 8.
- **Graphics API:** the game talks to the GPU through a **graphics API**
  (Vulkan, OpenGL ES, Metal). An old GPU without Vulkan shows a black screen
  if the build has no other path.
- **Screen shapes:** 20:9 phones with notches, 16:9 phones and 4:3 tablets
  need layouts anchored in the **safe area** (@fig-aspect).

A **compatibility matrix** records each test device and each check.
:::

![A compatibility matrix (example).](images/compat-matrix.png){#fig-compat width=94%}

![One menu, three screen shapes.](images/aspect.png){#fig-aspect width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 14.2 — Star Garden 2.0 on three devices"}
1. A phone with Android 7 cannot install it: the minimum is Android 8 (API
   26), so the store does not offer it on that phone.
2. An old tablet without Vulkan uses the OpenGL ES path of the build: the
   garden appears.
3. A 21:9 phone with a camera hole: the watering button sits inside the safe
   area and stays fully visible.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/compat-lab.html" poster="sims/compat-lab.png" title="Compatibility Lab: build 43 for every device" height="580" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Supporting every old device "for more players" without counting the cost.
Each older version and each graphics path adds testing; check how many
players really use them (market share, lecture 8).
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The matrix"}
In **Compatibility Lab**, make every row green. Write the cost of each
setting you changed.

*Your result:* three settings and their costs.

::: {.check}
Minimum Android 8 (API 26): the game must be tested on Android 8 too, and
avoid newer features. Vulkan + OpenGL ES: a second graphics path to test.
Menu anchored to the safe area: one more layout check per screen shape.
Then every row of build 43 is green.
:::
:::

## 14.3 Following developments with reliable sources

Platforms change every year. A tester must follow the changes
(@fig-sources).

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 14.3 — Following platform changes"}
- Read the **release notes** of new OS and engine versions: they list
  behaviour changes that can break a game.
- Prefer **reliable sources**: official documentation, release notes,
  benchmarks that explain their method, and your own written tests.
- Treat ads, forum rumours and undated posts as claims to check.
- After an update, run the test plan again on at least one updated device.
:::

![Where do performance facts come from?](images/sources.png){#fig-sources width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 14.3 — \"Twice the frame rate on old phones\""}
1. A video says that the new version of the game engine doubles the frame
   rate on old phones.
2. Rami reads the official release notes of the engine: they mention a
   faster loading of scenes, but no general speed-up.
3. Rami tests the new version on the P5 with the same race: the levels load
   2 seconds faster, the frame rate is the same. Rami writes the result in
   the test log, with the date.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Copying a number from a video into a report without its source and date.
A reliable report says where each number comes from.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · A release note"}
Find the release notes of the newest Android or iOS version on the official
developer site. Write two changes that could affect a game, with the source
and the date.

*Your result:* two changes with source and date.

::: {.check}
A good answer looks like: "developer.android.com, Android 16 behaviour
changes (read on 30 October 2026): 1. on tablets the system can ignore a
game that locks the screen to portrait, so the game must also work in
landscape; 2. background work has new limits, so the cloud save in the
background must be tested again." Check: an official page, the date you read
it, and two changes, each with what it means for a game.
:::
:::

## Case study: Performance Detective

Players of *Pocket Quest* send six reports: a race that jerks at 58 fps, a
hot phone that slows down after 15 minutes, a crash on Android 8, a black
screen on an old phone, a Start button cut off on a tablet, and a forum
claim about an OS update. The Game challenge of the interactive lesson uses
these reports. In the mini-game below you find the cause or the best fix
for each one.

{{< sim file="sims/perf-detective.html" poster="sims/perf-detective.png" title="Performance Detective: six player reports" kind="game" height="460" >}}

## Further reading

Android Developers, "Behavior changes" (for each Android version) and
"Support different screen sizes"; Apple Developer, "Human Interface
Guidelines: Layout". Check the date on each page.

## Exercises

1. What is the frame time of 60 fps?
2. Why is the 1 % low important, when the average is high?
3. Why must a performance test last as long as players play?
4. What does a frame-rate cap do?
5. Name the three causes of incompatibility of this lesson.
6. An old phone shows a black screen. What is a likely cause, and a fix?
7. What is a compatibility matrix?
8. Name two reliable sources for platform changes.
9. A forum says a new update makes every game faster. What do you do?
10. Why run the test plan again after an OS update?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. About 16.7 ms.
2. It shows the stutters that the player feels.
3. A hot chip slows down after some minutes (thermal throttling).
4. It limits the frame rate, so the load stays steady and the phone cooler.
5. The minimum OS version, the graphics API, the screen shapes.
6. The GPU does not support the graphics API (Vulkan); add an OpenGL ES
   path.
7. A table of test devices and checks, each marked pass or fail.
8. For example official release notes and developer documentation.
9. Read the official release notes and test it yourself.
10. The update can change behaviour that the game depends on.
:::
